newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hong Kong ends 156 years as a British colony with an emotional farewell for Governor Chris Patten and assurances that freedom wil survive under Chinese rule. (ALL PAPERS)

- President Fidel Ramos says the pursuit against members of kidnap-for-ransom syndicates in southern Mindanao will continue, virtually rejecting the demand of Moslem rebels to stop military operations in the area (MANILA STANDARD)
- Senator Raul Roco, a presidential aspirant, says he is launching his own party which will be an alliance of provincial and regional parties. (TODAY)
- Environment Secretary Victor Ramos says the Boracay resort island is "already a disaster case," warning tourists that the island is unsafe for recreational activities. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Noah's Ark group of companies and its foreign partners are considering buying the cash-strapped Victorias Milling Corp and its subsidiaries. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Duff and Phelps Credit Rating Co upgrades the country's foreign currency obligations by one notch to BB plus from BB. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The Central Bank projects inflation fell to 3.9 percent in June due to stable supply of prime commodities. (TODAY)
- KPPI Food Corp, a subsidiary of Kuok Philippine Properties Inc, will cease to operate effective July 31 as Kuok says it will focus more on real estate and property development. (MANILA STANDARD)
